children.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (form) is like a lump of foam; <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) is like a bubble;
<s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) is like a mirage; <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are like a plantain tree. (12)
For the wandering ascetic, the lustful man, and the dogs, regarding a single woman's body,

children.text: kuṇapaḥ kāminī bhakṣya iti tisro vikalpanāḥ || NagBhc_20
children.translated_text: [there arise the concepts:] 'a corpse,' 'a lover,' 'food' — three conceptualizations. (20)
For the purpose of eliminating the grasping of self, by the teaching of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and so forth —
even that [teaching] has been demolished by the great ones through the establishment of 'mind-only' (<s>cittamātra</s>). (25)

children.text: cittamātram idaṃ sarvam iti yā deśanā muneḥ |
children.translated_text: The teaching of the Sage that 'all this is mind-only' (<s>cittamātra</s>)
is for the purpose of dispelling the fear of the childish — it is not [the teaching of] ultimate reality. (27)
The <s>Tathāgatas</s> have not seen the mind as having the aspect of knower and known;

children.text: yatra boddhā ca bodhyaṃ ca tatra bodhir na vidyate || NagBhc_45
children.translated_text: where there is both a knower and a thing to be known, there <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) does not exist. (45)
Without characteristics, without arising, without abiding, beyond speech —

children.text: ākāśaṃ bodhicittaṃ ca bodhir advayalakṣaṇā || NagBhc_46
children.translated_text: space, <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), and <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) are characterized by non-duality. (46)

body.translated_text: All debaters are terrified by the lion's roar of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). (52)

children.text: guḍe madhuratā cāgner uṣṇatvaṃ prakṛtir yathā |
children.translated_text: Just as sweetness is the nature of molasses, and heat is the nature of fire,

children.text: śūnyatā sarvadharmāṇāṃ tathā prakṛtir iṣyate || NagBhc_57
children.translated_text: so <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is held to be the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. (57)
The teachings of the protectors of the world follow the dispositions of beings;

children.text: bhidyante bahudhā loka upāyair bahubhiḥ punaḥ || NagBhc_98
children.translated_text: they are divided in many ways in the world, again through many skillful means (<s>upāyas</s>). (98)
Distinguished as profound and accessible, sometimes having both characteristics,
though the teaching is divided, it is undivided — characterized by <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and non-duality. (99)
